42946-live-toys.creator: Emma Davenport,
42946-live-toys.description: A book by Emma Davenport,. first Pet that we ever remember possessing was a large white rabbit. We were then very little children; and, being at the sea-side, we spent the greater part of the day on the shore, or rather on the broad esplanade, that stretched for full half-a-mile round the pretty bay.

arxiv-1505-06247.creator: Gogi Pantsulaia, Khatuna Chargazia, Givi Giorgadze
arxiv-1505-06247.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Gogi Pantsulaia, Khatuna Chargazia, Givi Giorgadze. By using the method developed in the paper [G.Pantsulaia, G.Giorgadze, On some applications of infinite-dimensional cellular matrices, Georg. Tech., Nova Science Publishers, Volume 3, Issue 1 (2011), 107-129], it is obtained a representation in an explicit form of the particular solution of the linear non-homogeneous ordinary differential equation of the higher order whose coefficients are real-valued simple functions. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 34Axx ; Secondary 34A35, 34K06.

arxiv-1810-01876.title: Spurious samples in deep generative models: bug or feature?
arxiv-1810-01876.creator: Balázs Kégl, Mehdi Cherti, Akın Kazakçı
arxiv-1810-01876.description: Abstract Traditional wisdom in generative modeling literature is that spurious samples that a model can generate are errors and they should be avoided. Recent research, however, has shown interest in studying or even exploiting such samples instead of eliminating them.

arxiv-1904-02178.title: Universal quantum modifications to general relativistic time dilation in delocalised clocks
arxiv-1904-02178.creator: Shishir Khandelwal, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mischa P. Woods
arxiv-1904-02178.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Shishir Khandelwal, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mischa P. Woods. The theory of relativity associates a proper time with each moving object via its world line. In quantum theory however, such well-defined trajectories are forbidden. After introducing a general characterisation of quantum clocks, we demonstrate that, in the weak-field, low-velocity limit, all “good” quantum clocks experience time dilation as dictated by general relativity when their state of motion is classical (i.e.

arxiv-2105-07775.creator: Qian Li, Xiangmeng Wang, Guandong Xu
arxiv-2105-07775.description: Abstract . In recommendation systems, the existence of the missing-not-at-random (MNAR) problem results in the selection bias issue, degrading the recommendation performance ultimately. A common practice to address MNAR is to treat missing entries from the so-called “exposure” perspective, i.e., modeling how an item is exposed (provided) to a user.

arxiv-2305-00178.creator: Dorin Popescu
arxiv-2305-00178.description: Abstract . We show that an algebraic immediate valuation ring extension of characteristic p > 0 p>0 is a filtered union of complete intersection algebras of finite type. Key words : immediate extensions, pseudo convergent sequences, pseudo limits, smooth morphisms, complete intersection algebras. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 13F30, Secondary 13A18,13F20,13B40. arxiv-2308-10963.title: The Large Magellanic Cloud’s ∼ 30 \sim 30 Kiloparsec Bow Shock and its Impact on the Circumgalactic Medium Journal: ApJ Letters Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , yt ( Turk et al. 2011 ) , Enzo Bryan et al. 2014
arxiv-2308-10963.creator: David J. Setton, Gurtina Besla, Ekta Patel, Cameron Hummels, Yong Zheng, Evan Schneider, Munier Salem
arxiv-2308-10963.description: Abstract The interaction between the supersonic motion of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) and the Circumgalactic Medium (CGM) is expected to result in a bow shock that leads the LMC’s gaseous disk. In this letter, we use hydrodynamic simulations of the LMC’s recent infall to predict the extent of this shock and its effect on the Milky Way’s (MW) CGM.

arxiv-2401-06122.title: Manipulating Feature Visualizations with Gradient Slingshots
arxiv-2401-06122.creator: Dilyara Bareeva, Marina M.-C. Höhne, Alexander Warnecke, Lukas Pirch, Klaus-Robert Müller, Konrad Rieck, Kirill Bykov
arxiv-2401-06122.description: Abstract Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are capable of learning complex and versatile representations, however, the semantic nature of the learned concepts remains unknown. A common method used to explain the concepts learned by DNNs is Feature Visualization (FV), which generates a synthetic input signal that maximally activates a particular neuron in the network.

arxiv-2402-02961.title: GitBug-Java : A Reproducible Benchmark of Recent Java Bugs Conference: 21st International Conference on Mining Software Repositories; April 15–16, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal 21st International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR ’24), April 15–16, 2024, Lisbon, Portugal DOI: 10.1145/3643991.
arxiv-2402-02961.creator: André Silva ∗, Nuno Saavedra ∗, Martin Monperrus
arxiv-2402-02961.description: Abstract . Bug-fix benchmarks are essential for evaluating methodologies in automatic program repair (APR) and fault localization (FL). However, existing benchmarks, exemplified by Defects4J, need to evolve to incorporate recent bug-fixes aligned with contemporary development practices. Moreover, reproducibility, a key scientific principle, has been lacking in bug-fix benchmarks.

arxiv-2403-18273.title: Analysis of solution to an elliptic free boundary value problem equipped with a ‘bad’ data
arxiv-2403-18273.creator: Debajyoti Choudhuri, Shengda Zeng
arxiv-2403-18273.description: Abstract We will study a free boundary value problem driven by a source term which is quite irregular . In the process, we will establish a monotonicity result, and regularity of the solution. Keywords : Free boundary value problem, Hölder regularity, Monotonicity formula. AMS Classification : 35J35, 35J60.

arxiv-2502-08399.title: Ferromagnetic Resonance in a Magnetically Dilute Percolating Ferromagnet: An Experimental and Theoretical Study
arxiv-2502-08399.creator: Y.K. Edathumkandy ID, K. Das ID, K. Gas ID, D. Sztenkiel ID, D. Hommel ID, H. Przybylińska ID, M. Sawicki ID
arxiv-2502-08399.description: Abstract Ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) serves as a powerful probe of magnetization dynamics and anisotropy in percolating ferromagnets, where short-range interactions govern long-range magnetic order. We apply this approach to Ga 1-x Mn x N ( x ≃ 8 x\simeq 8 %), a dilute ferromagnetic semiconductor, combining FMR and superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry.

arxiv-2503-18302.title: DiffMove: Group Mobility Tendency Enhanced Trajectory Recovery via Diffusion Model PubID: pubid: 0000–0000 © 2025 IEEE
arxiv-2503-18302.creator: Qingyue Long, Can Rong, Huandong Wang, Shaw Rajib, Yong Li
arxiv-2503-18302.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Qingyue Long, Can Rong, Huandong Wang, Shaw Rajib, Yong Li. In the real world, trajectory data is often sparse and incomplete due to low collection frequencies or limited device coverage. Trajectory recovery aims to recover these missing trajectory points, making the trajectories denser and more complete. However, this task faces two key challenges: 1) The excessive sparsity of individual trajectories makes it difficult to effectively leverage historical information for recovery; 2) Sparse trajectories make it harder to capture complex individual mobility preferences.

arxiv-2508-14745.title: Intrinsic Linear Response from Zeeman Quantum Geometry in 2D Unconventional Magnets
arxiv-2508-14745.creator: Neelanjan Chakraborti, Sudeep Kumar Ghosh, Snehasish Nandy
arxiv-2508-14745.description: Abstract Unconventional magnets with zero net magnetization yet momentum-dependent spin splitting constitute a newly identified class of materials that provide a rich platform for quantum-geometry-driven transport phenomena. Exploiting the interplay between momentum translation and spin rotation, we uncover a distinct linear transport response governed by a generalized quantum geometric tensor, the Zeeman quantum geometric tensor (ZQGT).

arxiv-2510-11172.title: Developing an information criterion for spatial data analysis through Bayesian generalized fused lasso
arxiv-2510-11172.creator: Yuko Kakikawa
arxiv-2510-11172.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuko Kakikawa. In the field of spatial data analysis, spatially varying coefficients (SVC) models, which allow regression coefficients to vary by region and flexibly capture spatial heterogeneity, have continued to be developed in various directions. Moreover, the Bayesian generalized fused lasso is often used as a method that efficiently provides estimation under the natural assumption that regression coefficients of adjacent regions tend to take the same value.

arxiv-2512-02336.title: Forecasting MBTA Transit Dynamics: A Performance Benchmarking of Statistical and Machine Learning Models
arxiv-2512-02336.creator: Sai Siddharth Nalamalpu, Kaining Yuan, Aiden Zhou, Eugene Pinsky (corresponding author)
arxiv-2512-02336.description: Abstract The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) is the main public transit provider in Boston, operating multiple means of transport, including trains, subways, and buses. However, the system often faces delays and fluctuations in ridership volume, which negatively affect efficiency and passenger satisfaction.

pmc-10674638.title: New Perspectives about Drug Candidates Targeting HTLV-1 and Related Diseases
pmc-10674638.creator: Milena Cristina Martins da Silva, Renan Stefferson Barradas Pereira, Antonia Cherlly Aparecida Araujo, Ednilson Gregorio da Silva Filho, Anderson de Lima Dias, Kassio Silva Cavalcante, Maísa Silva de Sousa
pmc-10674638.description: Among the human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV) types, HTLV-1 is the most prevalent, and it has been linked to a spectrum of diseases, including HAM/TSP, ATLL, and hyperinfection syndrome or disseminated strongyloidiasis. There is currently no globally standard first-line treatment for HTLV-1 infection and its related diseases.

pmc-10742328.title: Imipramine Treatment Alters Sphingomyelin, Cholesterol, and Glycerophospholipid Metabolism in Isolated Macrophage Lysosomes
pmc-10742328.creator: Jacob M Albright, Matthew J Sydor, Jonathan Shannahan, Christina R Ferreira, Andrij Holian, Jorge Joven
pmc-10742328.description: Lysosomes are degradative organelles that facilitate the removal and recycling of potentially cytotoxic materials and mediate a variety of other cellular processes, such as nutrient sensing, intracellular signaling, and lipid metabolism. Due to these central roles, lysosome dysfunction can lead to deleterious outcomes, including the accumulation of cytotoxic material, inflammation, and cell death.

pmc-10750868.title: Transcatheter mitral valve repair clip embolization to the right coronary artery
pmc-10750868.creator: Jonathan Nitz, Manish Karamchandani, Tina Phan, Phil Carpino, Gregory Couper
pmc-10750868.description: Central Message Although rare, MitraClip embolization can be life-threatening. We report the treatment of 1 such case as the only survival to discharge in the literature. Although transcatheter mitral repair with MitraClip (Abbott) has been deemed a safe procedure for high-risk surgical populations, it does carry the possibility of complications.

pmc-11430808.title: Atypical Spindle Cell/Pleomorphic Lipomatous Tumor: A Review and Update
pmc-11430808.creator: Jun Nishio, Shizuhide Nakayama, Yoshiro Chijiiwa, Mikiro Koga, Mikiko Aoki
pmc-11430808.description: Simple SummaryAtypical spindle cell/pleomorphic lipomatous tumor (ASCPLT) is a novel entity of benign adipocytic neoplasm that can show variable CD34 immunoreactivity, loss of Rb expression, and RB1 gene deletion. Due to the rarity of the disease, ASCPLT remains poorly understood.

pmc-11615120.title: Identification of isoAsp7-Aβ as a major Aβ variant in Alzheimer’s disease, dementia with Lewy bodies and vascular dementia
pmc-11615120.creator: Sarah Schrempel, Anna Katharina Kottwitz, Anke Piechotta, Kathrin Gnoth, Luca Büschgens, Maike Hartlage-Rübsamen, Markus Morawski, Mathias Schenk, Martin Kleinschmidt, Geidy E. Serrano, Thomas G. Beach, Agueda Rostagno, Jorge Ghiso, Michael T. Heneka, Jochen Walter, Oliver Wirths, Stephan Schilling,
pmc-11615120.description: The formation of amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregates in brain is a neuropathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, there is mounting evidence that Aβ also plays a pathogenic role in other types of dementia and that specific post-translational Aβ modifications contribute to its pathogenic profile.

pmc-12467630.title: Linking Metabolic Disorders and Immune System Phenomena in Schizophrenia: The Role of Adipose Tissue and Inflammation
pmc-12467630.creator: Aleksandra Julia Oracz, Mateusz Zwierz, Maciej Naumowicz, Stefan Modzelewski, Maria Suprunowicz, Napoleon Waszkiewicz, Natalia V Gulyaeva
pmc-12467630.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Emerging evidence highlights the role of chronic low-grade inflammation and dysregulated cytokines in both obesity and schizophrenia, suggesting overlapping immune system pathways that contribute to cognition and nervous system inflammation. Excess adipose tissue functions as an active endocrine organ, releasing pro-inflammatory mediators that may serve as potential biomarkers, while the use of antipsychotic agents in schizophrenia further modifies cytokine profiles and immune responses.

pmc-13072127.title: Photodynamic Therapy-Based Strategies Targeted at Cancer Stem Cells: A Scoping Review
pmc-13072127.creator: Beatriz Serambeque, Inês Dias, Catarina Mestre, Carlos Miguel Marto, Maria Filomena Botelho, Maria João Carvalho, Mafalda Laranjo
pmc-13072127.description: Simple SummaryOne of the biggest challenges in cancer treatment is a small group of cells called cancer stem cells, which are often responsible for therapy failure, cancer spread, and recurrence after treatment. The goal of this review is to examine strategies for targeting cancer stem cells using photodynamic therapy.

pmc-13195026.title: Empowering researchers and healthcare professionals in academic publishing: key insights and practical lessons from the British Society of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy (BSAC) workshop 2025
pmc-13195026.creator: Godwin Pius Ohemu, Tsitsi Arikana Mufunde, Tracie Muraya, Emmanuel Essonanjo, Peter Zarb, Rasha Abdelsalam Elshenawy, Neil Powell, Virve I Enne, Riina Rautemaa-Richardson

pmc-13283002.title: A Rare Instance of Concordant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease and Familial Partial Lipodystrophy Type 2
pmc-13283002.creator: Mark A Bachir, Iyawnna Hazzard, Alexander S Bachir, Gavin Chima, Biljinder Chima
pmc-13283002.description: Lamin A/C (LMNA)-related laminopathies can involve adipose tissue, peripheral nerves, skeletal muscle, and the heart. We report a 65-year-old woman with a seven-year history of progressive distal sensorimotor neuropathy, burning pain in both feet, loss of hand dexterity, and worsening steppage gait.

pmc-13363919.title: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy as a Tool to Monitor Degradation, Fouling and Mechanical Damage in Ion-Selective Electrode Membranes
pmc-13363919.creator: Martyna Drużyńska, Nikola Lenar, Beata Paczosa-Bator
pmc-13363919.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) successfully distinguished between membrane fouling caused by environmental exposure and physical membrane damage in graphene-based Pb2+-selective ion-selective electrodes.River water and synthetic urine induced fouling-related changes in membrane morphology, roughness, and wettability, whereas mechanical damage produced a distinct electrochemical signature associated with loss of membrane integrity.
